title: 20. Phrasal verbs, idioms & figures of speech

q.t: What does give up mean in Never give up.?
q.e: give up = quit, stop trying.

q.t: Fill in: She ___ her baby brother while Mother was out. (took care of)
q.e: look after = take care of.

q.t: Fill in: I am ___ my lost pen. (searching)
q.e: look for = search.

q.t: What does a piece of cake mean?
q.e: An idiom: the test was a piece of cake = the test was very easy.

q.t: What does once in a blue moon mean?
q.e: A ‘blue moon’ is rare, so the idiom means very rarely.

q.t: Identify the figure of speech: She is as busy as a bee.
q.e: A comparison using ‘as … as’ → simile.

q.t: Identify the figure of speech: The wind whispered through the trees.
q.e: Wind can't whisper; giving it a human action → personification.

q.t: Identify the figure of speech: The bees buzzed.
q.e: ‘buzzed’ sounds like the noise bees make.

q.t: Fill in: The firemen ___ the fire. (extinguished)
q.e: put out = extinguish.

q.t: What does under the weather mean?
q.e: ‘I'm feeling under the weather’ = not well.

q.t: Fill in: The match was ___ because of rain. (cancelled)
q.e: call off = cancel.

q.t: Fill in: We have ___ sugar. Please buy some.
q.e: run out of = have none left.

q.t: Fill in: He ___ the job offer because the pay was low.
q.e: turn down = refuse.

q.t: Fill in: She ___ her father — both are tall and funny.
q.e: take after = resemble a parent.

q.t: What does let the cat out of the bag mean?
q.e: It means to tell a secret, often by mistake.

q.t: What does break the ice mean?
o: start a conversation in an awkward situation
q.e: ‘Breaking the ice’ makes people feel at ease.

q.t: Identify the figure of speech: The classroom was a zoo.
q.e: It says the room IS a zoo, with no ‘like’ or ‘as’ → metaphor.

q.t: Identify the figure of speech: I've told you a million times!
q.e: An obvious exaggeration for effect → hyperbole.

q.t: Identify the figure of speech: Sally sells sea shells.
q.e: The same first sound (s) repeated → alliteration.

q.t: What does cost an arm and a leg mean?
q.e: It means something costs a lot of money.

q.t: Fill in: The meeting was ___ till next week. (postponed)
q.e: put off = postpone.

q.t: Fill in: I ___ an old letter while cleaning the cupboard. (found by chance)
q.e: come across = find by chance.

q.t: Fill in: Our car ___ on the highway. (stopped working)
q.e: break down = stop working (of machines).

q.t: Fill in: Please ___ the meaning in the dictionary.
q.e: look up = find information in a book or list.

q.t: Identify the figure of speech: a deafening silence
q.e: Two opposite ideas (deafening, silence) side by side → oxymoron.

q.t: Identify the figure of speech: Who doesn't love a holiday?
q.e: A question asked for effect, expecting no answer.

q.t: What does burn the midnight oil mean?
o: work or study late into the night
q.e: It means staying up late to work or study.

q.t: What does hit the nail on the head mean?
q.e: To describe a problem exactly right.

q.t: What does in hot water mean?
q.e: ‘He's in hot water’ = he is in trouble.

q.t: Which is a simile, not a metaphor?
o: He has a heart of stone.
q.e: Only the first uses ‘like’ to compare.

q.t: What does a blessing in disguise mean?
o: something that seemed bad but turned out to be good
q.e: Missing the bus was a blessing in disguise — I met an old friend.

q.t: What does see eye to eye mean?
q.e: ‘They don't see eye to eye’ = they disagree.

q.t: Fill in: The two friends quarrelled but soon ___. (became friends again)
q.e: make up = become friends again (also: invent a story).

q.t: Fill in: She was ___ by her grandparents in a village. (raised)
q.e: bring up = raise a child.

q.t: Fill in: Don't ___ more than you can chew.
q.e: The idiom is ‘bite off more than you can chew’ = take on too much.

q.t: Identify the figure of speech: Water, water, everywhere, / Nor any drop to drink.
q.e: ‘Water’ is repeated for emphasis.

q.t: Identify the figure of speech: The stars danced playfully in the sky.
q.e: Stars can't dance or play — human actions given to things.

q.t: Identify TWO figures in: The thunder roared like a lion.
q.e: ‘like a lion’ = simile; giving thunder a lion's roar treats it as a living creature = personification.

q.t: What does the apple of one's eye mean?
q.e: ‘She is the apple of her grandfather's eye.’

q.t: Choose the meaning of He went through a lot of trouble.
q.e: go through = suffer or experience (also: examine carefully).
